city_vars.market_blurb: Lufkin, Texas serves as a key economic hub for East Texas, historically anchored by the timber and forestry industry due to its location in the Pineywoods region. The city's economy has diversified over time to include manufacturing—particularly oilfield equipment through companies like Lufkin Industries—along with healthcare and retail trade serving surrounding rural counties. As the largest city in Angelina County, Lufkin functions as a regional commercial and medical center.
city_vars.local_note: Lufkin's water supply, drawn largely from groundwater sources, tends to be moderately hard, which can contribute to mineral buildup in water heaters, dishwashers, and washing machines over time. The region experiences frequent severe thunderstorms and occasional tropical storm remnants from the Gulf, leading to periodic power surges and outages that can stress appliance electronics and compressors.
city_vars.city_spotlight:
Lufkin sits at the heart of the Piney Woods, serving as the commercial anchor for Deep East Texas and the seat of Angelina County. The surrounding forests built the city's original economy, and timber and wood products manufacturing still run deep in its identity, though the modern base has broadened considerably. Lufkin Industries' oil field equipment work, alongside healthcare, education, retail, and government offices, now gives the local economy a sturdier, more diverse footing than its lumber-town roots alone.

With roughly 34,000 residents, Lufkin feels sized just right — big enough for full-service hospitals, a community college, and steady employers, yet small enough that neighborhoods like Crown Colony and Kurth still carry a distinct, close-knit character. It's a working city, proud of its piney landscape and its role as the region's steady hub.

columns.heading: Not Freezing Cold Enough
columns.text: Your freezer may struggle to reach proper temperature due to a faulty thermostat, clogged vents, or a worn compressor. The local provider we connect you with will diagnose the root cause and restore your freezer's cooling power.

columns.heading: Ice Buildup Inside
columns.text: Excessive frost or ice accumulation often signals a defrost cycle failure or a blocked drain line. Our local repair partners can clear blockages and repair defrost components to prevent future buildup in your KitchenAid freezer.

columns.heading: Water Pooling or Leaking
columns.text: Leaks typically stem from a frozen or clogged drain, damaged water supply line, or a cracked drain pan. The independent technicians we partner with will locate the leak source and complete the necessary repairs.

columns.heading: Compressor Running Constantly
columns.text: If your freezer runs nonstop without cycling off, the compressor may be struggling, the thermostat could be faulty, or seals may be worn. Local providers we connect you with can test components and restore normal operation.

columns.heading: Loud Noises or Vibration
columns.text: Strange sounds or rattling often come from a failing fan motor, loose components, or compressor issues. The repair professionals in our network will identify the noise source and fix it to restore quiet operation.

columns.heading: Door Seal Not Closing Properly
columns.text: A weak seal lets cold air escape, forcing the freezer to work harder and waste energy. Our local partners can inspect the door gasket, check hinges, and replace worn seals to restore an airtight fit.

fq_items.question: What should I do if my KitchenAid freezer won't freeze properly?
fq_items.answer: First, check that the thermostat is set correctly and air vents inside aren't blocked by frost or food. If the freezer still won't reach the proper temperature, it likely needs professional service—common causes include refrigerant leaks, compressor failure, or a faulty thermostat. Contact Wells Appliance Repair to diagnose the issue before it worsens.
